A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELC study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A–E. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original benchmark results, component ablations, error analyses, and latency measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports an object-masking experiment on 100 images in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: The LLM fact extraction, visual grounding, task-specific logical inference, consistency metric, and aligned fusion procedures remain unchanged. The new masking experiment evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: NegBench COCO/VOC2007, HC-RefCOCOg, and HC-RefLoCo remain covered. V3 adds a 100-image scenario with critical objects manually masked, extending evaluation to altered visual input conditions.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same 11 MLLMs and the same LLM, VLM, and grounding-model alternatives in the appendices. The new masking example uses the already evaluated Qwen3.0-VL.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds original-versus-masked evaluation on 100 images, masking one critical object per image and reporting Acc50 and CR. Existing benchmark splits, IoU thresholds, and validation-based fusion alignment are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds a robustness test examining channel behavior when critical visual evidence is masked. The component, oracle-noun/box, fusion, and error analyses already existed in v2. The latency analysis is relocated rather than removed.

E5.justification: The correlation analysis and point-estimate reporting practices remain unchanged. V3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New masking results report Qwen3.0-VL ILC Acc50 falling from 91% to 60%, ELC Acc50 from 82% to 41%, and CR from 0.80 to 0.57. Existing table values are unchanged. V3's new CI summary quotes CR as 0.69, whereas the corresponding retained validation analysis reports 0.7027 in v2 supplementary Table 1 and v3 Table 6.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and inference/fusion formulas in Equations 1–13 are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: ELC, consistency-based validation and selection without ground truth, and performance enhancement through aligned fusion.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets ELC as more sensitive to missing referred objects. It also identifies WL outcomes as false negatives and asserts that CR is less affected by them. Most other added discussion summarizes interpretations already present in v2's appendix.

D1.justification: V3 provides limited preparation information for the new perturbation test: one critical object is manually masked per image. Existing prompts, model and hardware disclosures, dataset links, and timing information remain unchanged; the latency table is merely relocated.

R1.justification: The same 80 references and substantive positioning against earlier approaches are retained. Removing two generic sentences explaining joint embeddings and contrastive learning does not change the claimed relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: V3 adds main-text summaries of appendix analyses, relocates the latency discussion, and slightly shortens related-work background. It also updates author and affiliation text and adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2's supplementary latency Table 14 becomes main-text Table 5 in v3. Figure and table numbering becomes continuous across the document, with adjusted spacing and placement. Existing figure images and table contents are preserved.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves evaluation breadth through the object-masking test and makes existing computational costs and error analyses more visible in the main text. These gains are limited by sparse masking details and the new CI-summary discrepancy between CR 0.69 and the retained validation value 0.7027. The core scientific contribution and benchmark evidence remain stable.
